newsitem.title: USA: U.S. reaffirms concerns about Taleban.
newsitem.headline: U.S. reaffirms concerns about Taleban.

text.p: The United States reaffirmed on Wednesday it would not recognise the Taleban administration in Afghanistan and expressed renewed concerns about Taleban human rights policies, especially toward women and girls.

The comments by State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns reinforced the message that Assistant Secretary of State Robin Rafael gave earlier to Taleban militia leader Mullah Mohammed Omar during talks in the Pakistan capital, Islamabad.
The meeting was one of the highest-level contacts to date between Washington and the purist Islamic movement now ruling most of Afghanistan.
"We use our meetings to convey our concerns about the situation in Afghanistan. As you know, we don't recognise any of the factions as the legitimate government of Afghanistan," Burns told reporters.
"We have ongoing concerns regionally about neighbours of Afghanistan not funnelling arms to the factions. We'd like to see them resolve their severe problems peacefully," he said.

Burns added: "And we do take the opportunity in these meetings, as Assistant Secretary Rafael did today in Islamabad, especially with representatives of the Taleban, to note our very strong concerns about the human rights deficiencies of the Taleban regime, particularly concerning women and girls."
Rafael's meeting "is a part of our longstanding series of contacts and meetings that we've had not only with the Taleban, but with all of the factions in Afghanistan," Burns said.

The Taleban captured Kabul on Sept. 27, but no country has yet formally recognised their interim administration. The Taleban has been seeking to impose their strict version of Islam across Afghanistan.
Rafael will also be visiting Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and India.
